answer: We formulate a mechanism utilizing dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect slashing matrices to disincentivize Sybil identity multiplication. This design renders hollow capital fragmentation futile, as a beacon of zero-knowledge verifiable delay functions ensures slashing penalties scale non-linearly with attack complexity. Consequently, the continuous river of staking collateral creates a capital barrier where expected attack utility remains strictly negative, forcing convergence to a robust Nash equilibrium.
